question: What is the main activity restriction for the affected arm right after pacemaker insertion?

options.A: Avoid writing or holding objects with that hand
options.B: Keep the arm pressed tightly against the stomach
options.C: Do not raise the arm above shoulder height
options.D: Do not bend the elbow past ninety degrees

explanation: Lifting the arm too high can pull the newly placed wires loose from the heart muscle wall. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h4)

question: During which stage of pregnancy does heartburn usually act up the most?

options.A: Immediate postpartum
options.B: Third trimester
options.C: Implantation phase
options.D: First trimester

explanation: As the baby grows big and cozy in the third trimester, it pushes right up against the stomach, making acid reflux much more common.

question: Which of these grains is naturally safe to eat on a gluten-free diet?

options.A: Spelt
options.B: Barley
options.C: Rye
options.D: Quinoa

explanation: Quinoa is a fantastic pseudocereal that is naturally free of gluten. Perfect for safe and healthy meal planning!

question: Who are the best people to involve when mobilizing a local community for safer maternal health?

options.A: Factory owners and corporate bosses
options.B: Traditional rulers, religious leaders, and local community groups
options.C: Construction contractors and road engineers
options.D: International sports bodies and foreign embassies

explanation: Exactly! Local leaders have a huge influence on community health choices and are key partners in encouraging hospital deliveries.

question: What does high bioavailability mean for a medication?

options.A: The drug stays active in the body for many days.
options.B: A large amount of the active drug reaches the bloodstream.
options.C: The medication dissolves very slowly in cold water.
options.D: It is completely safe from causing any side effects.

explanation: High bioavailability means more of the active medicine is available to do its job in the body. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h3)

question: Which of these is a well-known chemical hazard you might find in a clinical area?

options.A: Discarded paper patient admission folders
options.B: Cardboard packaging from intravenous fluids
options.C: Used cotton wool rolls from wound dressing
options.D: Mercury from a broken blood pressure device

explanation: Correct! Heavy metals like mercury—often found in older BP cuffs or thermometers—are toxic chemicals that need careful cleanup if spilled.

question: Why is it risky to assume sudden confusion in an older adult is just 'normal aging'?

options.A: It automatically leads to permanent psychiatric institutionalization
options.B: It can cause nurses to miss acute illnesses like infections
options.C: It interferes with standard medication dosage calculations
options.D: It accelerates the natural hardening of the arteries

explanation: Great nursing insight! Never brush off sudden confusion as mere old age. It's often a red flag signaling a serious issue like a urinary tract infection or lack of oxygen.

question: Which skin antiseptic keeps working for hours after you apply it?

options.A: Glutaraldehyde
options.B: Sodium hypochlorite
options.C: Chlorhexidine gluconate
options.D: Isopropyl alcohol

explanation: Spot on! Chlorhexidine sticks to the skin and keeps killing bacteria long after you put it on, which is why we love it for surgical scrubs.

question: You are caring for a mother 2 hours after delivery. Which finding needs your immediate action?

options.A: Moderate fatigue and sleepiness following labor
options.B: Mild cramping pains while the baby is breastfeeding
options.C: A rapidly filling perineal pad with bright red blood
options.D: A temperature of 37.2 degrees Celsius

explanation: Well done! Heavy, soaking bleeding is a sign of postpartum hemorrhage—a true emergency that needs quick nursing intervention.

question: What is the key difference between formative and summative assessment?

options.A: Formative assessment guides ongoing learning, while summative assessment certifies final competence
options.B: Formative assessment is always graded, while summative assessment is optional
options.C: Formative assessment occurs at the end of a course, while summative assessment occurs at the start
options.D: Formative assessment tests physical skills, while summative assessment tests memory

explanation: Formative check-ins help you learn along the way, while summative tests (like finals) check if you've mastered the whole topic.

question: A nurse is caring for a bedridden patient with advanced Parkinson's disease. What is the best way to prevent bedsores (skin breakdown)?

options.A: Repositioning the patient every two hours
options.B: Keeping the room temperature very high
options.C: Encouraging the patient to run on a treadmill
options.D: Applying lotion once a week

explanation: Turning or repositioning the patient every two hours takes pressure off bony areas, keeping the skin safe and healthy. Excellent bedside care knowledge!

question: What is the very next thing you must do after the AED delivers a shock?

options.A: Check the carotid pulse for at least one full minute
options.B: Turn the machine off and wait for the ambulance crew
options.C: Remove the sticky pads and wipe the skin with alcohol
options.D: Resume chest compressions and CPR for two minutes

explanation: Right after a shock, don't wait—jump right back into CPR starting with chest compressions to keep blood moving!

question: What main feature separates hospital waste from ordinary rubbish at home?

options.A: It always smells much worse than domestic garbage
options.B: It is generated only by medical doctors and surgeons
options.C: It can be recycled directly without prior processing
options.D: It contains biological, chemical, and radioactive hazards

explanation: You got this! Healthcare waste needs special care because it carries dangerous germs and materials that can cause disease or injury—unlike normal house trash.

question: Which part of a homeostatic control system detects a change or stimulus in the environment?

options.A: Receptor
options.B: Control center
options.C: Set point
options.D: Effector

explanation: Receptors act as sensors that pick up changes in the environment and forward that data to the control center. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T10#GNS111_U1_T10_h2)

question: What is the main clinical purpose of performing basic anthropometric measurements in a hospital?

options.A: To measure the electrical activity of the heart
options.B: To evaluate nutritional status and help calculate drug doses
options.C: To diagnose specific infectious diseases quickly
options.D: To check how well the lungs exchange oxygen

explanation: Height and weight provide essential baseline numbers used directly to assess general health and safely figure out proper medication dosages. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T3#GNS112_U6_T3_h1)

question: An infusion pump starts beeping with a 'downstream occlusion' alarm. What should you check first?

options.A: The software version installed on the pump display
options.B: The IV tubing for kinks, closed clamps, or blockages
options.C: The main hospital electrical breaker panel in the hallway
options.D: The expiration date printed on the primary medication bag

explanation: That's correct! 'Downstream' means between the pump and the patient. Always check the line first for bends, pinches, or a closed roller clamp.

question: Why is keeping PAC patient information strictly confidential so important?

options.A: A breach of information can lead to severe social stigma or harm
options.B: The Nursing Council requires permanent archiving of all case notes
options.C: It prevents insurance companies from raising premium rates
options.D: Hospital accreditation depends entirely on zero medical errors

explanation: Because abortion carries heavy social stigma around us, a leaked secret can ruin relationships, jobs, or even put a patient's safety at risk.

question: Why do patients with multiple myeloma often suffer from severe bone pain?

options.A: Joint cartilage wears down completely from lack of fluid
options.B: Muscles pull too tightly on weak bones during movement
options.C: Nerves wrap tightly around damaged joints in the limbs
options.D: Malignant plasma cells expand inside the bone marrow cavity

explanation: Abnormal plasma cells build up inside the bones, increasing pressure and causing painful damage to the bone structure. You're doing great!

question: Which of these snacks is safest to give a toddler just as it is, without cutting it first?

options.A: A handful of roasted peanuts
options.B: Thinly sliced soft banana pieces
options.C: A whole hard candy lozenge
options.D: Whole raw baby carrots

explanation: Well done! Soft bananas mash up easily and don't pose the hard, sticky, or round risks that nuts, carrots, or candies do.

question: What is the main purpose of using the teach-back method?

options.A: To fulfill strict insurance billing rules
options.B: To confirm whether the patient truly understands the instructions
options.C: To give the nurse a break from talking
options.D: To test the patient's long-term memory capacity

explanation: Correct! Asking them to explain it back in their own words is the best way to make sure they got the right message.

question: Which family planning method protects against both pregnancy AND sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?

options.A: Hormonal implants
options.B: Copper intrauterine devices
options.C: Barrier methods
options.D: Natural fertility awareness

explanation: Great job! Barrier methods like male and female condoms block physical contact and fluids, giving you dual protection against both STIs and unwanted pregnancy.

question: What is the primary goal of using aseptic techniques during immunization?

options.A: To prevent the introduction of harmful pathogens into the body
options.B: To make the injection completely painless for the client
options.C: To speed up the total vaccination process
options.D: To ensure the vaccine liquid remains ice cold

explanation: Aseptic techniques are specifically designed to stop germs from contaminating sterile equipment and entering the client's body during a procedure. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h1)

question: What happens in the body during an episode of obstructive sleep apnea?

options.A: Repetitive collapse of the upper pharyngeal airway during sleep
options.B: Severe inflammation of the inner ear vestibular system
options.C: Permanent paralysis of the diaphragm muscle in the chest
options.D: Sudden accumulation of cerumen blocking the nasal passages

explanation: When the throat muscles relax too much during sleep, the airway temporarily collapses and closes. This causes loud snoring and sudden pauses in breathing. Rest easy knowing you understand this concept now!

question: What is the very first thing that happens when a person starts developing an illness?

options.A: Seeking medical care
options.B: Experiencing symptoms
options.C: Entering rehabilitation
options.D: Assuming the sick role

explanation: Easy and logical! The illness journey always starts when the person physically or mentally notices that something feels off in their body.

question: What HbA1c blood test result is generally used to diagnose diabetes?

options.A: 8.0% or higher
options.B: 10.5% or higher
options.D: 6.5% or higher

explanation: An HbA1c of 6.5% or higher shows that blood sugar has been running high over the past three months. It's a key lab value you'll use all the time in practice!

question: What does a high dependency ratio mean for a country?

options.A: Every citizen is completely financially independent.
options.B: The government has excess funds for infrastructure projects.
options.C: A small working-age population must support a large number of dependents.
options.D: There are more elderly people than working adults.

explanation: A high dependency ratio means fewer working adults are carrying the financial weight of supporting a large group of children and elderly dependents.

question: Why do birth attendants need to be extra careful if an episiotomy is done near vulval varicosities?

options.A: Dilated blood vessels tend to bleed much more heavily when cut
options.B: Cutting the skin will cause permanent nerve paralysis in the leg
options.C: Local anaesthetic injections will not work near swollen tissues
options.D: The wound will never heal properly due to poor local hygiene

explanation: Engorged veins are full of blood under pressure. Cutting near them requires extra caution because they can bleed quite heavily. You're building great clinical intuition!

question: A patient treated for a wasp sting allergy feels fine after 30 minutes and wants to go home. What should you tell them?

options.A: Explain that the patient must stay longer because a secondary reaction can happen hours later
options.B: Tell the patient that once symptoms stop, they will never have another reaction
options.C: Administer a second dose of epinephrine just to be completely safe before leaving
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately with a prescription for oral antihistamines

explanation: Allergic reactions can strike twice! We call this a biphasic reaction, meaning the patient needs to stick around for observation just in case symptoms return hours later.

question: What is a major consequence when young girls experience unplanned early pregnancies?

options.A: They receive free healthcare for the rest of their lives
options.B: They gain immediate leadership roles in politics
options.C: They automatically achieve financial independence
options.D: They are frequently forced to drop out of school

explanation: Unplanned early pregnancy is a leading cause of school dropout among young girls, restricting their future employment opportunities. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h4)

question: Why is a closed drainage system generally preferred over an open system?

options.A: It relies entirely on patient movement rather than gravity or suction
options.B: It never requires emptying or measuring by the nursing staff
options.C: It dissolves completely inside the body over a few days
options.D: It greatly reduces the chance of external bacteria entering the wound

explanation: Closed systems keep the drainage contained within sealed tubing and collection bags, making it harder for germs from the outside environment to reach the healing tissue. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h1)

question: What is the main reason a doctor performs a cystoscopy for suspected bladder cancer?

options.A: To directly view the bladder lining and take tissue samples
options.B: To measure the exact filtration rate of both kidneys
options.C: To flush out bacterial infections from the lower ureters
options.D: To check the blood level of prostate-specific antigen

explanation: A cystoscopy uses a thin, lighted tube passed through the urethra. It lets the doctor look right inside the bladder and grab a small tissue sample if something looks unusual.

question: Why should nurses pay close attention to the worries of hospitalized patients?

options.A: It allows the nurse to shorten the visiting hours for relatives
options.B: It guarantees that the patient will pay their medical bills on time
options.C: Patients prefer strict institutional schedules over personal freedom
options.D: Fear and powerlessness can negatively impact healing and compliance

explanation: Well thought out! When patients are too stressed or scared, it can actually slow down their physical recovery and make them less likely to follow treatment.

question: Which of these is strongly linked to developing primary bone cancer later in life?

options.A: Prior exposure to therapeutic ionizing radiation
options.B: Long-term bacterial infections of the joint space
options.C: Chronic dietary deficiency of calcium and vitamin D
options.D: High impact sports injuries during childhood

explanation: Previous radiation treatment for childhood cancers can unfortunately increase the risk of a secondary bone sarcoma down the road.

question: What does the term 'essential drugs' refer to in Primary Health Care?

options.A: Rare experimental drugs tested only on laboratory animals
options.B: Expensive imported cosmetics sold at private pharmacies
options.C: Life-saving medicines that satisfy the priority health needs of the population
options.D: Traditional herbs harvested secretly at midnight

explanation: Essential drugs are selected based on public health relevance, safety, and cost-effectiveness to treat common conditions. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h9)

question: What is the main goal of rehabilitation for patients with sensory organ disorders?

options.A: To completely cure the underlying physical organ pathology
options.B: To maximize remaining functional capacity and restore independence
options.C: To isolate the patient from environmental safety hazards
options.D: To replace lost sensory organs with synthetic alternatives

explanation: You've got this! Rehab isn't always about a 100% cure; it's about helping patients make the absolute best of the senses they still have so they can live life on their own terms.

question: Which of these body areas is a classic, go-to site for giving a subcutaneous injection?

options.A: The sole of the foot
options.B: The abdomen
options.C: The center of the chest
options.D: The palm of the hand

explanation: That's right! The abdomen is a favorite spot for everyday injections like insulin and heparin because it has a nice, accessible layer of fat.

question: What unusual color does urine often turn in a patient with Acute Glomerulonephritis?

options.A: Thick bright orange
options.B: Cola or smoky brown
options.C: Bright neon green
options.D: Milky white and cloudy

explanation: Because red blood cells break down as they pass through the inflamed kidneys, the urine ends up looking dark like Coca-Cola or smoky brown. A classic clinical sign!

question: What is the modern medical approach to non-urgent surgeries on intersex infants?

options.A: Delaying non-urgent procedures to protect bodily autonomy until the child can participate
options.B: Mandating hormone therapy immediately after birth
options.C: Ignoring the physical variation completely without any documentation
options.D: Performing immediate surgery on every infant to fix chromosomal imbalances

explanation: You got it! Modern medical ethics value a child's right to their own body, avoiding rushed, irreversible cosmetic surgeries.

question: Why is it smart to include family members in outpatient nutrition teaching?

options.A: Hospital rules require family presence for all visits
options.B: Family members often handle the shopping and cooking
options.C: Clients cannot remember any verbal instructions alone
options.D: Family members pay for the clinic services directly

explanation: Makes total sense! Since family members usually buy and cook the food, bringing them into the conversation ensures the plan actually happens at home.

question: What is the first thing a nurse should do right after a shock is delivered?

options.A: Resume chest compressions right away
options.B: Administer a routine dose of IV atropine
options.C: Draw blood samples for arterial blood gas analysis
options.D: Check the carotid pulse for up to one minute

explanation: Don't pause to check for a pulse immediately! Modern resuscitation rules tell us to jump right back into chest compressions to keep blood flowing.

question: Which of these is NOT a job of a professional nursing organization when it comes to ethics?

options.A: Promoting values like patient autonomy and justice
options.B: Drafting and updating the code of ethics for the profession
options.C: Issuing personal loans to nurses in financial distress
options.D: Guiding members on how to handle moral dilemmas

explanation: Professional bodies write our ethical codes and help us navigate tough clinical choices, but they don't operate as financial banks or loan providers.

question: What is the main purpose of doing a workplace risk assessment?

options.A: To evaluate how likely a hazard is to cause harm and determine appropriate controls
options.B: To replace all human workers with automated robotic machinery
options.C: To calculate the exact financial profit generated by each department
options.D: To find reasons to terminate employees who report minor injuries

explanation: Think of a risk assessment as looking ahead: we spot the danger, see how likely it is to hurt someone, and put rules in place to stop accidents before they happen.

question: What is a major advantage of the oral route of drug administration?

options.A: It is convenient and economical for the patient
options.B: It is completely safe for unconscious patients
options.C: It bypasses the liver completely
options.D: It works faster than intravenous injections

explanation: Swallowing pills requires no special sterile equipment and can easily be managed by conscious patients, making it cost-effective and convenient. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why must you write down any recent antibiotics the patient is taking on the lab request form?

options.A: The laboratory requires proof that the prescription was filled
options.B: Medications can affect microbial growth and test interpretation
options.C: Pharmacies will not process the sample without this record
options.D: It determines the financial cost billed to the patient

explanation: Antibiotics in the patient's system can stop germs from growing in the lab dish, so the lab needs to know so they don't misread a false negative!

question: Which breathing problem makes a cardiac bed necessary for a patient?

options.A: Bradypnea
options.B: Apnea
options.C: Orthopnea
options.D: Kussmaul breathing

explanation: Exactly! Orthopnea is when a patient struggles to breathe while lying flat, which is why cardiac patients need an upright bed setup.

question: What is the key sign of a post-dural puncture headache?

options.A: It gets worse when the patient sits up and improves when lying flat
options.B: It feels like a sharp electrical shock running down both legs
options.C: It stays at the exact same intensity regardless of body position
options.D: It only occurs during the night and disappears by afternoon

explanation: You nailed it! Low fluid pressure pulls on pain-sensitive areas when upright, which eases up when the patient lies horizontal.

question: Why is the final skin closure count so tricky if everyone is tired?

options.A: The anesthesia machine might lose electrical power
options.B: The hospital will run out of disposable suture packs
options.C: A missing item can easily be overlooked when fatigue sets in
options.D: The surgeon will finish the operation too quickly

explanation: Well reasoned! Long surgeries cause fatigue, making it extra important to stay sharp during the final count. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h4)

question: A lung cancer patient reports sudden back pain, weak legs, and trouble passing urine. What emergency should you suspect?

options.A: Tumor lysis syndrome
options.B: Spinal cord compression
options.C: Superior vena cava syndrome
options.D: Febrile neutropenia

explanation: Excellent clinical catch! Back pain plus weakness and bladder issues is a classic red flag for a tumor pressing right on the spinal cord.

question: What does the term 'total pain' mean in palliative care?

options.A: Pain that reaches the maximum possible score on a numerical rating scale
options.B: Pain caused exclusively by widespread metastatic cancer lesions
options.C: Pain that involves physical, emotional, social, and spiritual suffering
options.D: Pain that does not respond to any known pharmaceutical intervention

explanation: Total pain acknowledges that suffering in advanced illness goes beyond the physical body to include psychological, social, and spiritual components. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T14#GNS321_U4_T14_h1)

question: Which brain structure releases gonadotropin-releasing hormone to start the cycle?

options.A: Hypothalamus
options.B: Pituitary gland
options.C: Adrenal gland
options.D: Thyroid gland

explanation: The hypothalamus is the master control center that secretes gonadotropin-releasing hormone to trigger the pituitary gland. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h3)

question: A patient calls the clinic panicking because their stool turned dark green after starting iron pills. What should you tell them?

options.A: Advise them to stop taking the iron tablets immediately and rush to the hospital
options.B: Reassure them that this is a harmless and expected side effect
options.C: Tell them to collect a stool sample to check for bleeding
options.D: Tell them to drink less water because it dilutes the drug

explanation: No need to panic! Unabsorbed iron naturally turns the stool dark green or black as it passes through. Giving this quick reassurance eases patient anxiety instantly.

question: Which of these is considered a direct cause of maternal death?

options.A: Sickle cell anemia
options.B: Eclampsia
options.C: Severe malaria
options.D: Rheumatic heart disease

explanation: Eclampsia (severe pregnancy-induced high blood pressure leading to seizures) is a direct complication of pregnancy. The others are medical conditions made worse by pregnancy (indirect).

question: What is the most serious potential complication of an intraarticular injection?

options.A: Temporary skin bruising
options.B: Septic arthritis
options.C: Mild muscle soreness
options.D: Slight skin redness

explanation: Infection inside the joint space is a severe and dangerous complication requiring urgent medical treatment. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h8)

question: Before a solid pill can cross into the bloodstream, what must happen to it first?

options.A: It must pass through the kidneys first
options.B: It must reach the large intestine intact
options.C: It must combine with red blood cells
options.D: It must disintegrate and dissolve in fluids

explanation: Solid medicine can't just slip through cell walls as a hard chunk. It has to break apart and completely dissolve in fluid first!

question: Which emergency shows up as facial swelling, upper body congestion, and swollen neck veins because a major blood vessel is blocked?

options.A: Febrile neutropenia
options.B: Spinal cord compression
options.C: Tumor lysis syndrome
options.D: Superior vena cava syndrome

explanation: Awesome work! When a tumor presses on the superior vena cava, blood backs up from the upper body, causing that classic facial and neck swelling.

question: In simple terms, what is pharmacology?

options.A: The manufacturing process of chemical substances
options.B: The legal rules for selling prescription medicine
options.C: The history of herbal remedies and traditional cures
options.D: The study of how drugs interact with living systems

explanation: You've got this! Pharmacology is simply exploring how different chemical substances affect living tissues and organisms. Keep it up!

question: A patient comes in with swollen lower legs, brownish skin around the ankles, and a dull ache that gets worse when standing. What condition is most likely?

options.A: Raynaud's disease
options.B: Acute arterial blockage
options.C: Chronic venous insufficiency
options.D: Severe peripheral arterial disease

explanation: Those brownish marks, swelling, and tired aching legs are classic signs that blood is pooling in the lower legs because the veins are struggling to push it back up.

question: Why is it important to let the chest completely recoil (rise back up) between compressions?

options.A: It allows the heart chambers to refill with blood
options.B: It keeps the patient's airway open naturally
options.C: It gives the rescuer time to rest their arms
options.D: It prevents the ribs from fracturing

explanation: Full recoil lets the heart expand like a sponge so fresh blood can flow back in, ready for your next push.

question: What is the frontline, life-saving medication for treating a patient in anaphylactic shock from a sting?

options.A: Paracetamol
options.B: Amoxicillin
options.C: Hydrocortisone
options.D: Epinephrine

explanation: You got it! Epinephrine is the gold standard because it quickly fixes dangerously low blood pressure and opens up closed airways.

question: Why must you shake a suspension bottle vigorously right before pouring a dose?

options.A: To cool down the liquid inside the glass container
options.B: To evenly redistribute settled solid drug particles
options.C: To check if the outer safety seal is broken
options.D: To create air bubbles that make the drug taste better

explanation: Shaking mixes the active medicine back into the liquid so the patient gets the right dose, not just flavored water!

question: Why are older adults much more prone to bad drug interactions?

options.A: They experience reduced kidney and liver function along with polypharmacy
options.B: They routinely consume excessive amounts of herbal supplements
options.C: Their plasma protein levels are always abnormally elevated
options.D: Their digestive tracts absorb oral medications much faster than younger adults

explanation: As we age, our kidneys and livers don't clear drugs as quickly as they used to. Combine that with taking several medications at once, and drugs can easily build up to harmful levels.

question: What is the medical term for an infection of the lower urinary tract involving the bladder?

options.A: Glomerulonephritis
options.B: Urethral stricture
options.C: Pyelonephritis
options.D: Cystitis

explanation: Cystitis specifically refers to inflammation and infection of the urinary bladder, typically presenting with dysuria and frequency. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h1)

question: Which layer of the early placental membrane eventually thins out significantly or disappears in many areas by term?

options.A: Umbilical adventitia
options.B: Cytotrophoblast
options.C: Syncytiotrophoblast
options.D: Capillary endothelium

explanation: The cytotrophoblast layer thins out and becomes discontinuous as the placenta matures, bringing maternal and fetal blood vessels closer together. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h2)

question: What defines an immunization 'defaulter' child?

options.A: A child who experienced a severe allergic reaction to a vaccine
options.B: A child who completed all required immunizations ahead of time
options.C: A child who received an initial dose but missed subsequent scheduled doses
options.D: A child who has never received any vaccine at all

explanation: A defaulter started their immunization schedule but failed to return for booster or subsequent doses on time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h6)

question: If a nurse shines a light in an unconscious patient's eyes and both pupils stay large and don't react, what does that usually mean?

options.A: Dangerous pressure is affecting the brainstem
options.B: The patient is experiencing a mild concussion
options.C: Blood glucose levels are extremely elevated
options.D: The patient is entering a normal deep sleep cycle

explanation: Good catch! Fixed, unmoving pupils are a serious warning sign that pressure is squeezing the vital brainstem pathways.

question: How can pouring leftover drugs down open drains harm our environment?

options.A: It triggers severe volcanic activity near water bodies
options.B: It contributes to antimicrobial resistance and harms aquatic life
options.C: It instantly freezes local rivers and kills vegetation
options.D: It causes immediate radioactive contamination in the soil

explanation: Drugs in our waterways expose local water animals and bacteria to medications, helping drug-resistant superbugs grow faster.

question: Which common Nigerian food is a great plant-based source of protein?

options.A: Cassava tubers
options.B: Cowpeas (beans)
options.C: White yam slices
options.D: Ripe plantain fruits

explanation: Beans (cowpeas) are a fantastic, affordable local source of plant protein that helps build and repair body tissues.

question: What is often the most reliable early warning sign of an infection in a patient with a very weak immune system?

options.A: A mild or low-grade fever
options.B: Rapid weight gain
options.C: Severe localized pain
options.D: Large amounts of visible pus

explanation: Correct! Since other classic signs like pus or heavy swelling might not show up, a slight rise in temperature is often your first big clue that an infection is brewing.

question: What is the best way for a nurse to open a conversation about grief with a newly bereaved family member?

options.A: Advise them to stop crying and stay strong
options.B: Tell them everything happens for a good reason
options.C: Avoid mentioning the loss to prevent upsetting them
options.D: Ask open-ended questions about how they are coping

explanation: Open-ended questions give grieving individuals the safe space they need to express their true feelings. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h5)

question: What is the main imaging test doctors use to confirm osteoarthritis?

options.A: CT scan
options.B: Ultrasound
options.C: Bone scan
options.D: X-ray

explanation: Spot on! Standard X-rays are the quickest and most common way to check for narrow joint spaces and bone spurs.

question: What does holistic nursing care require nurses to address alongside physical needs?

options.A: Spiritual and emotional needs
options.B: Financial planning records
options.C: Dietary supplement costs
options.D: Legal guardianship papers

explanation: Holistic nursing looks at the entire person, which includes physical, emotional, and spiritual dimensions of health. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T13#GNS225_U5_T13_h1)

question: What is the collective term for all the external structures of the female reproductive system?

options.A: Vestibule
options.B: Vulva
options.C: Perineum
options.D: Introitus

explanation: The vulva is the medical term used to describe all the external female genital structures combined. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T2#GNS311_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why is inflammation affecting any layer of the heart considered a serious medical concern?

options.A: It exclusively affects the lungs and has no impact on circulation
options.B: It only causes temporary skin rashes on the chest wall
options.C: It can severely compromise the heart's ability to pump blood effectively
options.D: It instantly stops all electrical activity without warning

explanation: Swelling and damage to heart tissues disrupt the normal pumping action, which can lead to heart failure and poor circulation. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h1)

question: In social media culture, what does the popular acronym 'FoMO' stand for?

options.A: Frequency of mobile operation
options.B: Failure of modem output
options.C: Fear of missing out
options.D: Focus on major online

explanation: Ever felt uneasy logging off because something exciting might happen? That's FoMO—the nagging worry that everyone else is having fun online without you.

question: A community nurse gives out insecticide-treated bed nets to prevent malaria. Which part of the epidemiological triangle is this tackling?

options.A: The genetic makeup
options.B: The infectious agent directly
options.C: The environment
options.D: The host immune system

explanation: Great thinking! Bed nets change the environment where humans and mosquitoes meet, keeping the vector away from you.

question: Which of these is the main feature of a benign tumor?

options.A: It travels through the blood to distant organs
options.B: It has poorly differentiated cells
options.C: It remains localized and does not spread
options.D: It invades surrounding nearby tissues

explanation: You got it! Benign tumors stay put in one place. They don't invade nearby tissues or spread around the body like malignant ones do.

question: Why is checking the suction apparatus considered a critical step before beginning the intubation procedure?

options.A: To inflate the balloon cuff once the tube is in the trachea
options.B: To quickly clear vomit, blood, or secretions blocking the view
options.C: To measure the exact volume of air inside the patient's lungs
options.D: To deliver humidified oxygen straight down the breathing tube

explanation: Unforeseen fluids can instantly obscure the clinician's view of the vocal cords, making immediate suction essential for patient safety. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h2)

question: Which of these items is a classic biological hazard you'll encounter on the wards?

options.A: Empty food containers from the cafeteria
options.B: Cardboard boxes from office supplies
options.C: Blood-soaked dressings and swabs
options.D: Expired non-prescription tablets

explanation: Correct! Items dripping or soaked with blood or body fluids carry active germs that can easily cause infections if not handled carefully.

question: What is always the very first step in the community health planning cycle?

options.A: Assessment
options.B: Evaluation
options.C: Implementation
options.D: Budgeting

explanation: Spot on! Before you can help or build a program, you first need to assess and understand what is going on in the community.

question: What is a common psychological challenge many patients face after surviving a major cardiac event?

options.A: Complete memory loss regarding their entire hospital stay
options.B: Anxiety and fear about experiencing another heart attack
options.C: A sudden lack of interest in eating any food whatsoever
options.D: Aggressive behavior toward healthcare staff and family members

explanation: The trauma of a sudden heart attack often leaves patients feeling vulnerable, anxious, and fearful that physical activity will trigger another episode. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T13#GNS213_U1_T13_h6)

question: A postpartum mother had a very long labor and an emergency cesarean section. Which condition is she most at risk for developing?

options.A: Cervical polyps
options.B: Endometritis
options.C: Uterine prolapse
options.D: Ovarian cysts

explanation: Long labors and C-sections mean the uterus is exposed for a longer time, which greatly increases the risk of bacteria getting inside and causing endometritis.

question: Which of these is NOT a good strategy for promoting gender-sensitive nursing care?

options.A: Considering both biological factors and social pressures during assessment
options.B: Using respectful and inclusive language during patient history collection
options.C: Making automatic assumptions about a patient's health needs based purely on their gender
options.D: Advocating for equitable healthcare access across all segments of society

explanation: Spot on! Good nursing care means treating every patient as a unique individual, not making assumptions based on gender stereotypes.

question: What substance do the glands in your ear canal secrete to trap dust and bugs?

options.A: Synovial fluid
options.B: Cerumen
options.C: Saliva
options.D: Sweat

explanation: Cerumen is just the medical term for earwax! It acts as a natural shield protecting your delicate ear canal from dirt and bacteria.

question: Why do proton pumps in the collecting duct rely on primary active transport?

options.A: To push hydrogen ions against a very steep concentration gradient
options.B: To reabsorb all filtered glucose before it reaches the bladder
options.C: To prevent potassium from entering the urine under normal conditions
options.D: To move sodium ions passively alongside water molecules

explanation: Because the urine is already packed with acid, pushing more hydrogen ions in takes extra energy. That's why primary active transport uses direct energy to get the job done!

question: When should the nurse label the collected blood specimen tube?

options.A: At the bedside immediately after the blood draw
options.B: Inside the laboratory before handing it to the technician
options.C: At the nursing station after finishing all morning rounds
options.D: Before entering the patient room to save time

explanation: Labeling specimens at the bedside immediately after collection ensures proper patient identification and prevents mislabeling errors. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h5)

question: When is it legally and ethically okay for a nurse to share a patient's confidential abuse details?

options.A: At any time the nurse feels curious about the case details
options.B: When there is a mandatory legal requirement or imminent danger to life
options.C: Whenever family members demand information about the incident
options.D: When posting general hospital statistics on social media

explanation: Spot on! Patient privacy is sacred, but we must break confidentiality if someone's life is in immediate danger or the law requires mandatory reporting.

question: What is the purpose of flashing lights (photic stimulation) during an EEG?

options.A: To warm up the conductive paste on the scalp
options.B: To trigger abnormal brain waves using flashing lights
options.C: To measure how fast the pupils dilate in bright light
options.D: To help the client relax into a deep sleep state

explanation: Sometimes brains need a little nudge to show what they do under stress. Flashing lights at different speeds can help bring out hidden seizure patterns.

question: Why do young children get middle ear infections so much easier than adults?

options.A: Their tympanic membranes are thinner and easily ruptured
options.B: Their Eustachian tubes are shorter and more horizontal
options.C: They lack antibodies in their outer ear canals
options.D: They produce excessive earwax that traps bacteria

explanation: Well done! Because kids' Eustachian tubes lie flatter and shorter, germs and fluid slip easily from the throat right into the middle ear.

question: A patient with hearing loss is struggling to catch your discharge instructions. What should you do first?

options.A: Ask a family member to take over all patient care responsibilities
options.B: Face the patient directly and speak in a clear, moderate tone
options.C: Shout loudly from across the room so they can hear better
options.D: Stop talking and write everything down in complex medical terms

explanation: Spot on! Facing them lets them see your face and lip-read, which makes understanding much easier.

question: A patient having a blood transfusion suddenly develops fever, chills, and sharp lower back pain. What is likely happening?

options.A: Delayed iron toxicity
options.B: Circulatory fluid overload
options.C: Simple allergic skin rash
options.D: Acute hemolytic reaction

explanation: Lower back pain, fever, and chills are classic warning signs that the body is reacting against the red blood cells. Great clinical cue to remember!

question: Why is it so important for nurses to check in on a patient's mental health during post-abortion care?

options.A: Patients with mental distress are legally barred from receiving contraceptives
options.B: Psychological symptoms interfere directly with the absorption of oral antibiotics
options.C: Hospital insurance policies refuse to pay claims without a mental health diagnosis
options.D: Physical healing alone does not address hidden trauma, anxiety, and depression

explanation: Treating the physical body is only half the job. The secrecy and stress surrounding unsafe abortions leave deep emotional wounds that also need healing and gentle support.

question: How does a 'stimulation test' help us figure out an endocrine issue?

options.A: It forces the pancreas to stop making insulin during high stress
options.B: It tests if an underactive gland can produce hormones when given a trigger
options.C: It measures the permanent destruction of the pituitary stalk
options.D: It permanently blocks all hormone receptors in peripheral tissues

explanation: You're doing great! If a gland is acting lazy, we give it a special trigger (stimulation) to see if it still has the energy to wake up and produce hormones.

question: Why does severe anemia make mothers so vulnerable to dying from postpartum hemorrhage?

options.A: It prevents the placenta from forming correctly in the first trimester
options.B: It directly causes high blood pressure and seizures
options.C: It leaves women with very little physiological reserve to survive normal blood loss during delivery
options.D: It stops uterine contractions during the second stage of labor

explanation: Makes total sense when you think about it: if a woman is already low on blood (anemic), even normal blood loss during delivery can quickly throw her into shock. Always push for iron supplements during ANC!

question: Once the fetus produces waste, which organs of the mother ultimately clear and get rid of it?

options.A: Kidneys and liver
options.B: Lungs and skin
options.C: Gastrointestinal tract
options.D: Lymphatic system

explanation: You're right! Once the waste crosses over into the mother's blood, her own kidneys and liver do the heavy lifting to filter it out.

question: Why do doctors prescribe the steroid dexamethasone to hospitalized COVID-19 patients?

options.A: To dissolve existing blood clots in the lower legs
options.B: To stimulate the appetite and prevent severe weight loss
options.C: To suppress severe and damaging body inflammation
options.D: To kill the coronavirus directly inside the lungs

explanation: Correct! Dexamethasone helps calm down that over-enthusiastic immune response that wreaks havoc on the lungs.

question: What is a key nursing priority when taking a health history from a patient with possible tubal problems?

options.A: Checking daily blood pressure and cholesterol
options.B: Screening for bone density disorders
options.C: Testing the patient for gestational diabetes
options.D: Asking about past ectopic pregnancies and pelvic infections

explanation: Past infections and previous ectopic pregnancies give us vital clues about scar tissue or changes in the tubes. Keep up the great study habit!

question: Why do the cells on the very outer layer of your skin not have nuclei?

options.A: They have been damaged by direct exposure to ultraviolet radiation
options.B: They are specialized immune cells that do not require genetic material
options.C: They are actively dividing stem cells that have temporarily discarded their DNA
options.D: They are dead, keratin-filled cells that have been pushed upward from deeper layers

explanation: Exactly right! As skin cells travel up from the bottom, they flatten, fill with tough keratin, lose their nuclei, and form a protective dead layer.

question: Why do nurses mix cytotoxic drugs inside special safety cabinets?

options.A: To keep the sterile medication free from room dust
options.B: To warm the liquid solution before intravenous infusion
options.C: To speed up the chemical dissolution of the powder
options.D: To prevent accidental exposure from drug splashes or aerosols

explanation: Spot on! These cabinets protect you from breathing in tiny invisible droplets or getting splashes on your skin while mixing.

question: How do traditional beliefs often mischaracterize women who have not undergone FGM?

options.A: As being unable to bear healthy children
options.B: As being hypersexual and prone to promiscuity
options.C: As lacking basic community survival skills
options.D: As suffering from chronic physical weakness

explanation: Correct! Cultural myths wrongly claim that unoperated women cannot control their sexual urges.

question: What is the main goal of conducting a community diagnosis?

options.A: To enforce federal health laws and penalize local market vendors
options.B: To identify local health problems and community assets systematically
options.C: To diagnose individual patients visiting the tertiary hospital ward
options.D: To calculate the exact hospital budget required for surgery units

explanation: Instead of looking at one patient, a community diagnosis looks at the whole town to find out what health challenges they face and what resources they already have.

question: Why would a doctor order a diagnostic thoracentesis?

options.A: To measure how much oxygen the lungs can hold total
options.B: To find out the exact cause of a pleural fluid buildup
options.C: To prevent the development of a future heart attack
options.D: To permanently cure chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

explanation: Great thinking! When we take a little sample of that fluid to the lab, we can figure out why it started gathering in the chest in the first place.

question: Why do standard precautions apply to every single patient in the ward, even those not diagnosed with an infection?

options.A: Patients get offended if healthcare workers wear gloves only for some beds
options.B: Some patients may carry infections without showing any symptoms yet
options.C: Hospital management requires it only for statistical record keeping
options.D: It is too difficult for nurses to remember different rules for different people

explanation: Standard precautions assume any body fluid can carry pathogens because asymptomatic carriers can transmit infections unknowingly. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h4)

question: A farm worker comes in with excessive drooling, tearing, sweating, and diarrhea after spraying crops. What type of poisoning is most likely?

options.A: Cholinergic
options.B: Sympathomimetic
options.C: Sedative-hypnotic
options.D: Anticholinergic

explanation: Fantastic clinical deduction! Organophosphate pesticides cause over-stimulation of the parasympathetic system—remember the helpful SLUDGE mnemonic for all those wet secretions!

question: Why are ACE inhibitors or ARBs frequently prescribed for nephrotic syndrome?

options.A: They prevent bacterial infections in the urinary tract
options.B: They completely cure the underlying autoimmune disease
options.C: They replace lost albumin directly in the bloodstream
options.D: They decrease pressure inside the glomerulus to reduce protein leakage

explanation: These medications relax the tiny blood vessels leaving the glomerulus, lowering the pressure that forces protein out into the urine. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h4)

question: Why do pregnant women often experience frequent urination?

options.A: The ascending colon expands
options.B: The abdominal aorta shifts
options.C: The right kidney grows larger
options.D: The urinary bladder gets squeezed

explanation: Spot on! Because the female bladder sits right below the uterus, a growing pregnancy means less room for the bladder to store urine. You'll see this a lot in clinical rotations!

question: What is a major limitation of relying solely on prevalence studies?

options.A: They are completely illegal to conduct in rural community settings
options.B: They can be affected by survival bias, missing those who died quickly
options.C: They cost more money than any other form of scientific research
options.D: They only measure future health risks and ignore current problems

explanation: Prevalence only counts current survivors, missing individuals who died rapidly before being surveyed. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h7)

question: In diabetic neuropathy, how do we classify burning pain versus numbness?

options.A: Burning pain is an autonomic symptom, while numbness is a motor system deficit
options.B: Both burning pain and numbness are classified as positive motor symptoms
options.C: Both burning pain and numbness are classified as negative sensory symptoms
options.D: Burning pain is a positive sensory symptom, while numbness is a negative sensory symptom

explanation: Remember: 'positive' means the nervous system is adding an extra sensation (like pain or tingling), while 'negative' means a function is missing or lost (like numbness).

question: A patient with thick mucus cannot clear their throat and shows signs of airway blockage. What immediate nursing action is required?

options.A: Asking the patient to hold their breath for one minute
options.B: Placing the patient flat on their back to rest
options.C: Suctioning the airway to remove the trapped secretions
options.D: Administering a dose of blood pressure medication

explanation: When a patient cannot cough up mucus blocking their airway, suctioning physically clears the passage so air can flow. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h4)

question: How does food intoxication differ from a food infection?

options.A: Intoxication only affects the upper respiratory system
options.B: Infection has a much shorter incubation period
options.C: Infection is caused strictly by chemical pollutants
options.D: Intoxication results from pre-formed toxins in the food

explanation: Think of food intoxication as getting sick from poisons that bacteria already made inside the food before you ate it, leading to very fast symptoms!

question: Which item is essential to include in a basic home emergency supply kit?

options.A: Decorative scented candles
options.B: Large collection of reading books
options.C: Extra television remote controls
options.D: Flashlight and clean drinking water

explanation: During power outages or natural disasters, safe drinking water and light sources are vital for basic survival and safety. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h8)

question: What is the medical term for seeing double, which happens when the nerves controlling eye movement are messed up?

options.A: Mydriasis
options.B: Ptosis
options.C: Diplopia
options.D: Strabismus

explanation: Diplopia is just the clinical word for double vision. It occurs when the tiny muscles around the eyes aren't working together smoothly.

question: What is a major financial advantage of home health care over hospital admission?

options.A: It avoids expensive daily hospital room charges and facility overhead costs
options.B: It guarantees a monthly financial stipend for the patient's family
options.C: It makes all medical supplies and prescription drugs completely free
options.D: It removes the need for health insurance policies entirely

explanation: Eliminating hospital room and board fees significantly lowers the overall cost of treatment. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h3)

question: Which injection site is generally considered the safest for adult patients?

options.A: Deltoid
options.B: Dorsogluteal
options.C: Ventrogluteal
options.D: Vastus lateralis

explanation: The ventrogluteal site lacks major nerves and large blood vessels, making it the preferred and safest choice for adults. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h2)

question: Which of the following describes economic violence in a domestic relationship?

options.A: Splitting utility bills evenly between two working adults
options.B: Forgetting to consult a partner before making a household purchase
options.C: Donating family savings to a charity without asking
options.D: Controlling access to money and preventing a partner from working

explanation: Economic abuse involves financial control, making the survivor entirely dependent on the abuser for survival. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h2)

question: When is the best time to introduce palliative care to a cancer patient?

options.A: Early alongside active disease treatment to improve quality of life
options.B: Only when the patient refuses to take prescribed oral medications
options.C: Only during the final twenty-four hours of life
options.D: After all chemotherapy and radiation treatments have failed completely

explanation: Palliative care isn't just for the end of life—it teams up with curative treatments from day one to keep the patient comfortable. Excellent holistic nursing!

question: How does asking senior nursing mentors for feedback help you grow as a student?

options.A: It prevents patients from ever filing complaints against the hospital
options.B: It provides an outside perspective on communication strengths and blind spots
options.C: It replaces the need to study theoretical nursing models
options.D: It guarantees an automatic promotion to head nurse

explanation: Mentors have walked the path before you. Their advice helps you spot things in your bedside manner that you might not notice on your own.

question: What structure marks the point where nerve fibers exit the eye to form the optic nerve?

options.A: Optic disc
options.B: Pupil
options.C: Retina
options.D: Macula

explanation: The optic disc is the anatomical convergence point where nerve fibers leave the eye and appears as a yellowish-pink structure during the exam. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h2)

question: What is the main job of endocrine glands in our body?

options.A: Filtering waste products out of liquid blood
options.B: Secreting hormones directly into the bloodstream
options.C: Producing digestive enzymes for the stomach
options.D: Pumping oxygenated blood to body tissues

explanation: Spot on! Endocrine glands don't use ducts. They release their chemical messengers (hormones) straight into nearby blood vessels to reach organs all over the body.

question: What is the primary site for nutrient absorption in the human body?

options.A: Stomach
options.B: Small intestine
options.C: Esophagus
options.D: Large intestine

explanation: The small intestine has specialized structures that provide a massive surface area specifically designed for taking in digested nutrients. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T7#GNS121_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is the main job of carbohydrates in our bodies?

options.A: Producing protective antibodies for immunity
options.B: Transporting fat-soluble vitamins in blood
options.C: Providing the main source of daily energy
options.D: Repairing damaged muscle tissues and bones

explanation: You got it! Carbs break down into glucose, which is your brain's and muscles' favorite and most efficient fuel for the day.

question: What does 'active participation' mean when conducting a community health session?

options.A: Only community leaders are allowed to ask questions
options.B: The community is involved rather than just listening passively
options.C: Nurses must do all the talking during every session
options.D: Patients are required to pay a fee before learning

explanation: Active participation means learners engage directly with the material through questions and actions, which helps them remember and change behaviors better.

question: What makes an injection truly safe in healthcare?

options.A: It causes no harm to the patient or healthcare worker
options.B: It costs less than oral medications
options.C: It is performed only by senior doctors
options.D: It is always administered in the gluteal muscle

explanation: Spot on! A safe injection protects everyone—the patient getting treated, you as the healthcare worker, and our community from hazardous waste.

question: Which condition causes facial swelling, neck vein bulging, and trouble breathing due to a blocked major vein?

options.A: Spinal Cord Compression
options.B: Superior Vena Cava Syndrome
options.C: Febrile Neutropenia
options.D: Tumor Lysis Syndrome

explanation: When a tumor presses on the superior vena cava, blood gets backed up in the upper body, causing that distinct facial swelling. Spotting this makes you a sharp nurse!

question: A student practices passing a urinary catheter three times on a dummy before doing it on a real patient. What is this called?

options.A: Intrinsic motivational grading
options.B: Passive cognitive observation
options.C: Pedagogical dependency
options.D: Deliberate practice and skill repetition

explanation: Repeating a skill in a safe practice space builds your muscle memory and boosts your confidence for real clinical work.

question: Why do patients need X-rays or scans before starting cervical traction?

options.A: To prove the patient has health insurance
options.B: To find out the patient's favorite neck position
options.C: To measure the exact weight of the patient
options.D: To check for hidden bone weakness or instability

explanation: Imaging acts like a roadmap so the healthcare team can make sure there are no surprises like hidden fractures before applying traction.

question: A labouring mum has strong contractions, but the baby's head is quite large. What natural process helps the foetal skull pass through her pelvis?

options.A: Expansion of the maternal pelvic bones to match the skull
options.B: Rapid fusion of the fontanelles to make the head rigid
options.C: Immediate closure of the sagittal and coronal sutures
options.D: Overlapping of the cranial bones at the sutures

explanation: When things are a tight squeeze, the cranial bones do a clever trick called overlapping at the suture lines to temporarily shrink the head circumference.

question: What is the primary goal of family planning when it comes to maternal health?

options.A: To replace the need for routine antenatal checkups
options.B: To increase the total birth rate in rural areas
options.C: To space pregnancies and prevent high-risk births
options.D: To completely eradicate all infectious diseases

explanation: Spot on! Family planning gives women control over their pregnancies, helping them avoid very young or older high-risk ages and keeping healthy gaps between kids.

question: What is the safest way for a nurse to check the strength and timing of a mum's contractions?

options.A: Ask the patient to guess how long her abdominal pain lasts
options.B: Measure the mother's blood pressure before and after every contraction
options.C: Perform frequent digital vaginal examinations every fifteen minutes
options.D: Palpate the fundus of the uterus with the fingertips over a set period

explanation: Gentle touch on the top of the uterus (the fundus) tells you everything you need to know about contractions without risking infection from too many internal exams.

question: Which of these is a physical, non-drug method to help ease pain?

options.A: Teaching the patient to meditate
options.B: Applying a cold pack to a fresh sprain
options.C: Suggesting an antidepressant
options.D: Giving a dose of oral paracetamol

explanation: Using physical items like heat packs, cold packs, or gentle massage are great non-drug ways to soothe sore tissues.

question: What is the main goal when a patient with chronic Hepatitis C is given direct-acting antiviral medications?

options.A: To temporarily relieve itching caused by high blood pressure
options.B: To replace the damaged liver tissue with artificial cells
options.C: To boost the patient's appetite and promote rapid weight gain
options.D: To cure the infection and prevent long-term liver scarring

explanation: Modern medicines are wonderful—these direct-acting antivirals aim to completely kick the Hepatitis C virus out of the body and stop further damage.

question: What does finding chorioamnionitis on a delivered placenta tell you?

options.A: Maternal gestational hypertension
options.B: A normal physiological aging process of the placenta
options.C: An intrauterine bacterial infection of the fetal membranes
options.D: A previous cesarean section scar

explanation: Chorioamnionitis means bacteria got into the amniotic sac, which is a red flag that both mum and baby need to be watched closely for signs of infection. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h5)

question: What does the ethical principle of autonomy mean for an older patient?

options.A: The duty of the nurse to do no harm
options.B: The obligation to tell the truth at all times
options.C: The fair distribution of medical resources
options.D: The right to make their own healthcare decisions

explanation: Autonomy refers to a person's independence and right to self-determination regarding their medical care. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T1#GNS321_U3_T1_h6)

question: A patient with a blocked bowel feels strong, crampy tummy pain that comes and goes in waves. What causes this?

options.A: Total relaxation of the intestinal smooth muscle due to nerve damage
options.B: Strong peristaltic waves trying to push intestinal contents past the physical blockage
options.C: Acid erosion of the stomach lining caused by prolonged fasting
options.D: Rapid bacterial multiplication creating sudden localized inflammation in the liver

explanation: That colicky pain happens because the gut muscles are working extra hard, squeezing forcefully against the blockage to move food along.

question: What is the standard treatment to cure a benign primary heart tumour?

options.A: High-dose radiation therapy alone
options.B: Strict bed rest and fluid restriction
options.C: Surgical excision
options.D: Long-term oral antibiotic therapy

explanation: Since it's a physical mass, the best way to deal with a benign heart tumour is to surgically cut it out. Clean and effective!

question: Why is it important for nurses to use standard nutritional terms?

options.A: It allows nurses to cook meals for patients.
options.B: It prevents dangerous misunderstandings among the healthcare team.
options.C: It completely replaces the need for blood tests.
options.D: It speeds up the hospital discharge process.

explanation: Great job! Using clear, standard words means doctors, nurses, and dietitians are all on the same page, keeping your patients safe.

question: How does metabolic stress differ from simple starvation?

options.A: Metabolic stress lowers the heart rate to save body nutrients.
options.B: Metabolic stress forces high energy use while blocking normal tissue conservation.
options.C: Simple starvation causes sudden swelling all over the body.
options.D: Simple starvation causes a faster breakdown of muscle than major trauma.

explanation: While simple starvation triggers energy-saving mechanisms, inflammatory metabolic stress forces continuous tissue breakdown without letting the body conserve resources. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T023#GNS227_U2_T023_h3)

question: What is the main goal of Youth Friendly Services (YFS)?

options.A: To provide free medical treatment only for children
options.B: To attract and address the health needs of adolescents
options.C: To make hospitals run faster and more efficiently
options.D: To replace adult medical care entirely

explanation: You got it! YFS is all about creating a safe space tailored to the unique physical and emotional needs of young people.

question: What is the document used by staff to track when medications are given to residents?

options.A: Maintenance repair schedule
options.B: Medication administration record
options.C: Facility financial balance sheet
options.D: Daily dietary menu log

explanation: The medication administration record, or MAR, is the official document used to track every dose of medication given to a resident. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h5)

question: During a school health screening, you notice a female student is pale, always tired, and struggling in class. What should be your immediate nursing action?

options.A: Expel the student immediately to prevent the spread of fatigue to other pupils
options.B: Prescribe over-the-counter multi-vitamins without checking her medical history
options.C: Report the parents to the local police department without gathering further data
options.D: Conduct a comprehensive health assessment including nutritional screening and inquiry into home life

explanation: Always start with a proper assessment! Finding out if it's poor nutrition, anemia, or stress at home helps you give the right support before jumping to conclusions.

question: Which nursing action helps ensure an accurate blood pressure reading during a screening clinic?

options.A: Using a cuff that is much smaller than the patient's arm circumference
options.B: Allowing the patient to chat actively while the cuff inflates
options.C: Taking the measurement immediately after the patient jogs up the stairs
options.D: Ensuring the patient's arm is supported at heart level with feet flat on the floor

explanation: Proper positioning prevents muscle tension and gravitational artifacts that can falsely raise blood pressure readings. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h6)

question: What happens to total maternal serum calcium levels during a normal pregnancy?

options.A: They decrease due to hemodilution and lower albumin
options.B: They increase significantly to support fetal bone growth
options.C: They remain completely unchanged throughout all trimesters
options.D: They drop dangerously low because of kidney failure

explanation: Total serum calcium drops because blood volume expands and blood protein levels fall, but ionized calcium stays normal. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h3)

question: Why do many people in local communities prefer getting injections from informal medicine shops?

options.A: Oral medications are completely unavailable in cities
options.B: Government policy requires informal shops to give shots
options.C: They believe injections work much faster than pills
options.D: Injections are always cheaper than tablets

explanation: It's a common belief that shooting medicine straight into the body heals you faster than swallowing a pill. As nurses, patient education on safe administration is key here!

question: What is happening inside the heart chambers during diastole?

options.A: The ventricles squeeze blood into the arteries
options.B: The electrical signals stop moving entirely
options.C: The chambers relax and fill with blood
options.D: The heart valves completely disappear

explanation: Diastole is the resting phase! The heart muscle relaxes so that blood can flow in and fill up the chambers, getting ready for the next big squeeze.

question: A patient has a kidney stone stuck right where the ureter crosses the major blood vessels near the pelvis. What is this spot called?

options.A: The pelvic brim crossing
options.B: The vesicoureteral junction
options.C: The internal urethral orifice
options.D: The ureteropelvic junction

explanation: Well done! This is the second natural narrow point, right where the ureter crosses the pelvic brim.

question: What does normal, healthy cerebrospinal fluid look like?

options.A: Dark amber like strong tea
options.B: Bright red like fresh blood
options.C: Clear and colorless like water
options.D: Cloudy yellow like thin milk

explanation: Spot on! Normal CSF is transparent and looks just like clean water because it lacks blood cells or excess protein.

question: How do birth spacing and family planning help break the cycle of anaemia?

options.A: They remove the need for postpartum hygiene care.
options.B: They stop babies from getting birth defects.
options.C: They cure genetic blood disorders.
options.D: They give the mother's body time to rebuild iron stores before the next pregnancy.

explanation: Giving the body time to recover between babies prevents mom's iron and nutrient levels from staying dangerously depleted.

question: What is the best way to determine a patient's prior knowledge about a new medication?

options.A: Asking open-ended questions
options.B: Ordering a blood electrolyte panel
options.C: Reading their bank statements
options.D: Checking their vital signs

explanation: Open-ended questions invite patients to share what they understand in their own words without feeling tested. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T7#GNS215_U4_T7_h3)

question: Why does obstetric fistula often cause women to face social isolation in their communities?

options.A: Patients lose their ability to speak after the injury
options.B: Continuous incontinence leads to severe social stigma and shame
options.C: Government laws require isolation of all surgical patients
options.D: Traditional healers forbid them from leaving their homes

explanation: Because of constant leaking of urine or stool, affected women often face heartbreaking stigma and misunderstanding from their communities. As nurses, our empathy and care are crucial in supporting and healing them.

question: What do we call weakness affecting one entire side of the body, often seen after a stroke?

options.A: Monoparesis
options.B: Hemiparesis
options.C: Quadriplegia
options.D: Paraplegia

explanation: You got it! 'Hemi' means half, and 'paresis' means weakness—a classic clinical term to remember for your exams and wards.

question: What is the main goal of teaching a family home care after treating a patient for head lice?

options.A: To prove that the nursing staff performed their duties correctly
options.B: To prevent reinfection and spread among household members
options.C: To force the family to cut their hair short for safety
options.D: To ensure the patient buys the most expensive commercial products

explanation: Good teaching helps families clean bedding and check everyone else, stopping the lice from spreading right back to the patient! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h6)

question: Which imaging test uses a special dye to check if the Fallopian tubes are open?

options.A: Scrotal Doppler ultrasound
options.B: Pelvic magnetic resonance imaging
options.C: Hysterosalpingography
options.D: Transvaginal ultrasound

explanation: Brilliant! Hysterosalpingography involves putting dye into the uterus and taking X-rays to see if the fluid flows nicely through open Fallopian tubes.

question: What is the main goal of teaching a community about choking prevention?

options.A: To eliminate the sale of all round food items in local grocery stores
options.B: To ensure families purchase expensive medical safety equipment
options.C: To train every citizen to perform complex surgical procedures at home
options.D: To empower caregivers with knowledge to prevent incidents before they occur

explanation: Exactly! Teaching families how to spot risks and fix food shapes helps stop emergencies before they even start. Prevention is our best tool!

question: What is the official definition of reproductive health according to the broader health context?

options.A: The total absence of sexually transmitted infections in an adult population
options.B: A government program aimed at controlling population growth rates
options.C: A state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being in all matters of the reproductive system
options.D: The biological ability to conceive and bear children without medical help

explanation: Reproductive health covers total physical, mental, and social wellness regarding the reproductive system, rather than just lacking disease. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why must a nurse warm up a patient's cold hand before attaching a finger pulse oximeter probe?

options.A: Cold fingers have too much nail polish on them
options.B: Cold skin burns out the delicate infrared lights inside the sensor
options.C: Cold fingers prevent the patient from sitting still during the test
options.D: Cold temperatures cause vasoconstriction, reducing blood flow to the fingers

explanation: Poor peripheral circulation from coldness reduces pulse volume, making it hard for the machine to detect a clear signal. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h5)

question: Why is it helpful for fathers to attend child growth monitoring sessions?

options.A: They must record the child's weight in the main register.
options.B: They can help spot early signs of malnutrition.
options.C: They are required to administer the routine vaccines.
options.D: They prevent the mother from asking questions.

explanation: Growth charts let fathers clearly see how their child is developing and catch nutrition issues early.

question: According to Kübler-Ross, which stage of grief happens when a person tries to make a deal with God or fate to change what is happening?

options.A: Acceptance
options.B: Anger
options.C: Denial
options.D: Bargaining

explanation: In the bargaining stage, people try to negotiate or make promises to try and postpone or reverse an inevitable loss. You've got this!

question: If a partner stops you from working and controls all the money in the house, what kind of abuse is that?

options.A: Emotional abuse
options.B: Economic abuse
options.C: Sexual abuse
options.D: Physical abuse

explanation: Correct! Economic abuse happens when someone cuts off another person's access to money or financial independence to trap them.

question: Which of the following is NOT something a food safety supervisor needs to check?

options.A: Observing proper handwashing compliance
options.B: Monitoring refrigerator and freezer temperatures
options.C: Checking employee credit history records
options.D: Inspecting the safe storage of raw and cooked food

explanation: An employee's financial history has nothing to do with food safety! Inspections focus purely on hygiene and temperature control.

question: What is the maximum recommended time for a single suction pass?

options.A: 3 to 5 minutes
options.B: 1 to 2 minutes
options.C: 30 to 45 seconds
options.D: 10 to 15 seconds

explanation: Limiting passes to 10 to 15 seconds prevents the patient from running out of oxygen and developing dangerous heart rhythms. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h5)

question: What is the main goal of family planning right after delivery?

options.A: Eliminating all postpartum bleeding immediately
options.B: Ensuring the immediate return of normal menstruation
options.C: Speeding up the physical involution of the uterus
options.D: Preventing closely spaced and unplanned pregnancies

explanation: Postpartum family planning helps mothers space out their pregnancies, giving their bodies time to recover and protecting the health of both mom and baby! You've got this.

question: Which type of evidence is usually the least reliable when checking if a health treatment really works?

options.A: Personal testimonials and individual success stories
options.B: Peer-reviewed scientific journal articles
options.C: Randomized controlled clinical trials
options.D: Systematic reviews of multiple research studies

explanation: You got it! Personal stories and individual testimonials can be very biased, making them much weaker than structured clinical research.

question: A patient is assessed as a high fall risk. Which nursing action is best to keep them safe?

options.A: Remove all pillows from the bed to reduce soft surface risks
options.B: Ensure the bed is in the lowest position with the call bell close by
options.C: Keep the room lights completely off to encourage deep sleep
options.D: Encourage the patient to walk alone to the bathroom frequently

explanation: Keeping the bed low reduces injury if they fall, and keeping the call bell close means they can easily ask for your help before trying to get up!

question: A patient has delivered two full-term babies, had one early miscarriage, and has two living children. What is her parity?

options.A: Three
options.B: Four
options.C: Two
options.D: Five

explanation: You've got this! Parity counts pregnancies that made it past 20 weeks (viable births). Since she had two full-term deliveries, her parity is 2.

question: A nurse notices that many clients referred for long-acting methods never arrive at the general hospital. What practical step can she take to improve follow-up?

options.A: Increase the price of family planning commodities at her clinic
options.B: Scold clients publicly during clinic meetings for failing to travel
options.C: Stop referring clients altogether and attempt the procedures at the primary post
options.D: Engage community health workers to counsel and track referred clients

explanation: Community health workers can visit clients at home to address fears, answer questions, and encourage them to complete their referrals. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h8)
